stemMd: Why are small gaps often left between sections of a metal structure exposed to temperature changes?

options.label: A
options.textMd: To allow thermal expansion without excessive stress

options.label: B
options.textMd: To convert thermal energy directly into electricity

options.label: C
options.textMd: To make the metal lose all mass when heated

options.label: D
options.textMd: To ensure the metal's temperature never changes

explanationMd: Most metals expand on heating. Providing space accommodates dimensional change and reduces stress or buckling when sections would otherwise press against one another.

distractorRationale.d: The structure remains exposed to temperature changes.
distractorRationale.e: A gap does not eliminate every transfer mechanism.
distractorRationale.b: That is not the purpose of an expansion gap.
